title: Recognition of summand pullbacks from a disjoint sheaf partition
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and use the big fppf site [def-pc-fppf-site] and size convention [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $I$ be a small set, let $H$ and $(G_i)_{i\in I}$ be sheaves of sets [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], and let $c_i:G_i\to H$ be sheaf morphisms. Assume that $c_i:G_i(V)\to H(V)$ is injective for every $i,V$, and that, whenever $i\ne j$, $s\in G_i(V)$, $t\in G_j(V)$ and $c_i(s)=c_j(t)$, the scheme $V$ is empty. Let $T$ be a site object, let $(T_i)_{i\in I}$ be pairwise disjoint open and closed subschemes [def-weil-open-immersion] covering $T$, and let $a_i\in G_i(T_i)$. There is a unique $a\in H(T)$ satisfying $c_i(a_i)=a|_{T_i}$ for all $i$. For this $a$, if another clopen partition $(V_i)_{i\in I}$ and sections $t_i\in G_i(V_i)$ satisfy the same equations, then $V_i=T_i$ as open subschemes and $t_i=a_i$ after this identification. Put $h_W(Z)=\operatorname{Mor}_S(Z,W)$. For each $i$, the map
$$h_{T_i}(Z)\longrightarrow\{(b,s):b:Z\to T,\ s\in G_i(Z),\ c_i(s)=b^*a\},\qquad d\longmapsto(\iota_i d,d^*a_i)$$
is a bijection natural in every site object $Z$, where $\iota_i:T_i\hookrightarrow T$ is the inclusion. Thus $h_{T_i}\simeq h_T\times_HG_i$ as presheaves, with the fibre product on $Z$ defined by the displayed set, and with $a:h_T\to H$ given by $b\mapsto b^*a$. For every $b:Z\to T$, the inverse images $b^{-1}(T_i)$ and pullbacks of $a_i$ form the unique such partition and sections mapping to $b^*a$. These assertions allow empty pieces and $I=\varnothing$.

Agent formulation for arbitrary sectionwise injective, pairwise disjoint sheaf morphisms with a supplied clopen partition, including uniqueness, restriction and converse gluing.

proof.text: Every open covering occurring below is an fppf covering: its inclusions are etale by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale], hence flat and locally of finite presentation by [def-weil-etale-morphism], and their images cover, as required by [def-pc-fppf-site]. In particular the empty family covers the empty scheme. The equalizer definition of sheaf [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] then says that every set sheaf has exactly one section over an empty scheme: both products for that covering are singleton sets.

source.place: Tag 021L, definition-fppf-covering; morphisms.tex Tag 02GP, lemma-open-immersion-etale; sites.tex Tag 00VM, definition-sheaf-sets, and remark-sheaf-condition-empty-covering

proof.text: Set $u_i=c_i(a_i)\in H(T_i)$. For $i\ne j$ the intersection $T_i\cap T_j$ is empty, so Step 1 makes the two restrictions of $u_i,u_j$ equal there; for $i=j$ they agree by functoriality. Applying the equalizer condition [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] to the covering $(T_i\to T)_i$ gives a unique $a\in H(T)$ with $a|_{T_i}=u_i$. This uses no assertion about coproducts of sheaves.

source.place: Tag 00VM, definition-sheaf-sets; the compatible-family formulation following the definition

proof.text: Suppose $(V_i,t_i)_i$ is another partition and family for this same $a$. On $W=T_i\cap V_j$ the images of $a_i|_W$ and $t_j|_W$ in $H(W)$ are both $a|_W$. If $i\ne j$, the disjointness hypothesis on $c_i,c_j$ forces $W$ to be empty. As the $V_j$ cover $T$, every point of $T_i$ therefore lies in $V_i$. Reversing the roles of the two partitions gives $V_i\subseteq T_i$. Thus their underlying opens agree, and their open subscheme structures agree by [def-weil-open-immersion]. On this common scheme, $c_i(a_i)=a|_{T_i}=c_i(t_i)$; sectionwise injectivity of $c_i$ gives $a_i=t_i$.

source.place: Tag 0F15, lemma-coproduct-sheaves-open-and-closed, omitted verification; explicit comparison of two supplied partitions

proof.text: Fix a test scheme $Z$ and a pair $(b,s)$ in the displayed fibre set for index $i$. For every $j$, give the open subset $Z_j=b^{-1}(|T_j|)$ its open subscheme structure [def-weil-open-immersion]. The image of $b|_{Z_j}$ lies in $T_j$, so [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-factors-through-open-subscheme] gives a unique $S$-morphism $q_j:Z_j\to T_j$ over $b$. The $Z_j$ cover $Z$. By naturality, in $H(Z_j)$ we have $c_i(s|_{Z_j})=(b^*a)|_{Z_j}=q_j^*(a|_{T_j})=c_j(q_j^*a_j)$. For $j\ne i$ the disjointness hypothesis forces $Z_j$ to be empty. Hence $Z=Z_i$ as open subschemes, so $b(Z)\subseteq T_i$. Apply the same factorization lemma to obtain the unique $d:Z\to T_i$ with $\iota_i d=b$. It is over $S$ since its composite with $T_i\to T\to S$ is the given structure map of $Z$. Finally $c_i(s)=b^*a=c_i(d^*a_i)$, so injectivity gives $s=d^*a_i$.

source.place: Tag 0F15, lemma-coproduct-sheaves-open-and-closed: omitted verification that the open represents the summand pullback; schemes.tex Tag 01HI, lemma-restrict-map-to-opens

proof.text: Conversely, for $d:Z\to T_i$, naturality gives $c_i(d^*a_i)=d^*c_i(a_i)=(\iota_i d)^*a$, so the formula in the statement lands in the required fibre set. Step 4 recovers exactly $d$, by uniqueness of the factor through the inclusion; and Step 4 shows that every pair $(b,s)$ is the image of that recovered $d$. Thus this is a bijection. For any test morphism $r:Z'\to Z$, the image of $dr$ is $(\iota_i dr,(dr)^*a_i)=((\iota_i d)r,r^*(d^*a_i))$, exactly the restriction of the image of $d$. The bijections are therefore natural. The maps $a:h_T\to H$ and $a_i:h_{T_i}\to G_i$ used here are the explicitly natural rules $b\mapsto b^*a$ and $d\mapsto d^*a_i$; the natural bijections give the claimed isomorphism of presheaves.

source.place: Tag 0F15, lemma-coproduct-sheaves-open-and-closed, omitted pullback verification; naturality and the two inverse formulas

proof.text: For an arbitrary $b:Z\to T$, without a section $s$ prescribed, the inverse-image opens $Z_i=b^{-1}(|T_i|)$ are pairwise disjoint and cover $Z$. They are closed as well because their complements are inverse images of the open complements of $T_i$. With the maps $q_i:Z_i\to T_i$ constructed in Step 4, their sections $q_i^*a_i$ satisfy $c_i(q_i^*a_i)=(b^*a)|_{Z_i}$. Step 3 applied on $Z$ proves uniqueness of this partition and these sections. Step 2 applied to any supplied partition on $Z$ proves the corresponding converse gluing. Empty pieces cause no exception by Step 1. If $I=\varnothing$, the assumed covering of $T$ forces $T$ empty, its unique section is supplied by Step 1, partition uniqueness is vacuous, and there are no indices for the pullback assertions. Any $b:Z\to T$ then has empty source, so the base-change assertion also holds.

The item writes out exactly that verification, as old parent steps 6/7/8, with nothing shortened. Step 1: open immersions are etale (leaf), hence flat and lfp (def-weil-etale-morphism), so open covers are fppf covers; the empty family covers the empty scheme, so every set sheaf has a singleton section there by the equalizer condition. Step 2: equalizer gluing, using T_i x_T T_j = T_i cap T_j, which is empty for i different from j. Step 3: on T_i cap V_j the two labels have equal images, so disjointness makes it empty; hence V_i=T_i, and injectivity gives t_i=a_i. Step 4: Z_j=b^{-1}T_j, q_j comes from the open-factorization leaf, and c_i(s|Z_j)=c_j(q_j^*a_j) forces Z_j empty for j different from i; so b=iota_i d, which is over S, and s=d^*a_i. Step 5: inverse by uniqueness of the factorization, naturality by composition, and the presheaf fibre product is the one the statement defines. Step 6: the inverse-image partition is clopen, Step 3 applies on Z, and I empty forces T empty. Every cited proof dependency is a definition or a Mathlib leaf, so the route is fine and no tool_uses are needed. Edge cases checked: I empty, empty pieces, empty Z, two-point T=pt+pt, infinite I.
